title: BRIDGE X Youth Exposure Programme 2026: One-Year Leadership and Social Impact Opportunity for Undergraduate Students
summary: BRIDGE X 2026 is a year-long youth exposure programme by BRAC designed to give undergraduate university students practical exposure to development work, social innovation, social business, and leadership. The programme is intended for students who want to move beyond classroom learning, engage with real-world social challenges, and develop the skills, confidence, and networks needed to contribute to meaningful change. Through a structured journey involving practical problem-solving, professional development, campus engagement, and interaction with development practitioners, selected students, known as BRIDGE X focals , will have the opportunity to connect their academic knowledge with practical action. The programme offers an opportunity for young people to understand how development organisations approach complex social challenges while also encouraging participants to bring their own ideas, perspectives, and initiatives to their university campuses and wider communities. BRIDGE X 2026 at a Glance Programme: BRIDGE X Organiser: BRAC Duration: One year Target participants: Undergraduate university students Academic level: Primarily students in their second or third year Academic discipline: Any discipline Focus areas: Social development, social impact, social innovation, leadership, professional development and youth engagement Format: A combination of planned sessions, workshops, practical activities, problem-solving, and campus engagement Role: BRIDGE X focal Application process: Online application, take-home assessment and interview Deadline: 26 August 2026 Application: Applicants should use the official BRIDGE X application portal provided by BRAC. BRAC describes the initiative as an opportunity for undergraduate students to gain access to its wider ecosystem of solutions and develop a closer understanding of what it takes to become part of the next generation of leaders who can drive positive social change. What Is the BRIDGE X Programme? BRIDGE X is structured around the idea of creating a bridge between academic knowledge and practical action . University education can provide students with theoretical knowledge, analytical frameworks, and technical skills. However, understanding how social problems operate in real communities and how organisations design solutions to those problems often requires practical exposure. BRIDGE X seeks to provide that exposure. Participants will have opportunities to explore development challenges, work on cases related to social development, engage with practitioners, and contribute to conversations about important social issues. They will also be encouraged to bring these conversations back to their campuses through awareness activities, seminars, workshops, and other initiatives. The programme therefore combines several dimensions of youth development: Practical learning Professional development Leadership development Social impact exposure Campus engagement Networking Career exploration Rather than being limited to conventional classroom-based learning, the programme is designed to expose students to the realities of working on complex social and development challenges. Why BRIDGE X Is an Important Opportunity for University Students Students interested in development, international affairs, social innovation, public policy, communications, community development, business, sustainability, and related fields can benefit from opportunities that allow them to understand how ideas are translated into action. BRIDGE X provides such exposure by encouraging participants to examine real development problems and think about potential solutions. The programme can help students understand: How development organisations approach social challenges. How social innovation can contribute to solving complex problems. How social businesses operate within development ecosystems. How young people can contribute to social change. How to communicate important social issues within university communities. How professional networks can support future career development. How academic knowledge can be applied to real-world situations. What early-career pathways may exist within the development sector. For students considering careers in development organisations, international organisations, NGOs, social enterprises, research institutions, or other impact-oriented organisations, this type of exposure can provide valuable insight into the sector. Key Benefits of BRIDGE X 2026 1. Practical Exposure to Social Development One of the central benefits of BRIDGE X is the opportunity to gain exposure to development practice. Participants will work with cases and challenges grounded in real social development issues. This can help them move from simply studying social problems to thinking critically about how solutions can be designed and implemented. The experience can strengthen practical skills such as the following: Problem-solving Critical thinking Research Idea development Communication Collaboration Leadership Presentation Social impact analysis 2. Opportunity to Explore Social Impact BRIDGE X gives students an opportunity to explore the broader world of social impact. Participants can gain exposure to areas including development practice, social innovation, and social business, helping them understand how organisations attempt to create sustainable solutions to social challenges. This is particularly relevant for students who want careers where professional work is connected to social and community outcomes. 3. Networking and Professional Connections Networking is another important element of the programme. Selected participants will have opportunities to connect with: Fellow university students Development practitioners BRAC professionals Other young people interested in social change Potential professional contacts Learning and conference opportunities Building relationships at university can be particularly valuable because many future opportunities are developed through professional networks, peer communities, and exposure to practitioners. 4. Professional and Career Preparation BRIDGE X is also intended to help participants prepare for their future careers. Students can gain insight into workplace expectations and early-career pathways while developing experience that may strengthen their future applications. The programme may be particularly useful for students who are still exploring what type of career they want to pursue after university. Participants can use the experience to better understand: Their professional interests Their strengths and capabilities The development sector Social-impact careers Leadership opportunities Potential internship pathways Early-career opportunities 5. Potential Future Career Opportunities Participation in BRIDGE X does not automatically guarantee an internship or employment opportunity with BRAC. However, the programme is designed to provide experience and visibility that may be useful when participants later pursue internships or early-career opportunities. Students interested in BRAC s work can therefore use the programme as an opportunity to better understand the organisation and the types of professional environments within the development sector. BRAC separately operates a BRIDGE Internship Programme aimed at developing young talent for the development sector, demonstrating the organisation s broader interest in creating pathways for emerging professionals. 6. Becoming a BRAC Campus Focal Selected participants will serve as BRIDGE X focals and will have a role in representing BRAC on their campuses. This responsibility gives participants an opportunity to develop practical leadership experience. Focals can contribute to: Raising awareness of social challenges. Organising campus conversations. Supporting seminars and workshops. Encouraging students to engage with development issues. Sharing information about relevant career opportunities. Bringing youth perspectives into development discussions. This campus-facing role can help participants strengthen their communication, coordination, leadership, and event-management abilities. What Will BRIDGE X Participants Do? The programme gives participants several responsibilities throughout the year. 1. Solve Development Challenges Participants will be presented with development cases and asked to provide ideas and potential solutions. This component encourages students to apply analytical and creative thinking to real-world challenges. Students may need to consider: What the underlying problem is. Who is affected by the problem. Why existing approaches may not be sufficient. What possible interventions could address the issue? How a proposed solution could create meaningful impact. What challenges might affect implementation? This practical approach can help students develop a more solution-oriented mindset. 2. Represent Youth Perspectives Globally Participants may have opportunities to participate in global conferences or sessions where they can represent youth perspectives. This can expose students to broader conversations around development and social change and potentially introduce them to international learning and networking environments. For students interested in global development, international cooperation, or youth leadership, this aspect of the programme may be particularly valuable. 3. Activate the University Campus BRIDGE X participants will be encouraged to bring development conversations to their campuses. They may do this through: Seminars Workshops Awareness sessions Student discussions Other campus-based activities The objective is to help make social issues part of wider conversations among university students. 4. Contribute to New Development Initiatives Participants are also expected to provide youth perspectives and ideas that can contribute to the development of new initiatives. This gives young people an opportunity to move beyond being recipients of information and become contributors to conversations about development solutions. 5. Represent BRAC on Campus As BRIDGE X focals, selected students will help represent BRAC and increase awareness of the organisation s work and career opportunities among students. This responsibility requires participants to demonstrate professionalism, communication skills and the ability to engage constructively with their peers. Who Is BRIDGE X 2026 Designed For? BRIDGE X is specifically designed for undergraduate university students , particularly those who are currently in their second or third year of study . The programme is not restricted to one academic discipline. Students from any discipline can be considered, provided they demonstrate the interest, initiative, and engagement expected by the programme. The ideal applicant is not simply someone who performs well academically. BRIDGE X is particularly interested in students who are already demonstrating an interest in social development through activities outside the classroom. This can include participation in: University clubs Student organisations Community initiatives Volunteer activities Social-impact projects Leadership activities Other co-curricular engagements Qualities of a Strong BRIDGE X Applicant A competitive applicant should be able to demonstrate genuine curiosity, initiative, and an interest in making a positive contribution to society. Strong candidates are likely to be students who: Are interested in the development sector Applicants should demonstrate curiosity about social development and an interest in understanding how development organisations work. Have demonstrated social or community involvement Previous involvement in community activities, volunteering, social initiatives, or student-led projects can demonstrate that an applicant is already taking action rather than simply expressing an interest in social change. Want to explore purposeful careers The programme is suitable for students who want to understand how their education could eventually translate into a career focused on social impact. Are willing to take initiative Because participants are expected to activate their campuses and contribute ideas, initiative is an important characteristic. Are motivated to lead change BRIDGE X is aimed at students who want to contribute to change both within and beyond their university environment. Academic Discipline Requirements BRIDGE X does not appear to limit participation to a particular field of study. The programme explicitly describes itself as being for students from any discipline . This means that students studying subjects such as Social sciences International relations Development studies Economics Business Communications Public policy Law Education Technology Engineering Environmental studies Health Humanities Natural sciences and other academic fields may potentially find the programme relevant. The important consideration is the student s interest in social development, demonstrated initiative, and willingness to participate in the programme. The BRIDGE X Selection Process BRAC has outlined a three-stage selection process for BRIDGE X. Stage 1: Online Application The first stage is the online application. Applicants will be asked to provide information about their: Interests Experiences Motivation Engagement with social issues Interest in making change happen Applicants should therefore treat the application as more than a basic registration form. A strong application should clearly demonstrate why the applicant is interested in BRIDGE X and provide concrete examples of initiative, community involvement, leadership or social-impact activities. Stage 2: Take-Home Assessment Applicants who progress through the initial stage will complete a take-home assessment designed specifically for the programme. This stage is likely to provide applicants with an opportunity to demonstrate their thinking and problem-solving abilities. Applicants should approach the assessment carefully and demonstrate the following: Logical reasoning Creativity Understanding of the issue presented Practical thinking Clear communication Evidence-based reasoning where appropriate Feasible solutions Stage 3: Interview Shortlisted candidates will proceed to an interview. The interview provides an opportunity for the selection team to understand the applicant s motivation, personality, experiences, and suitability for the programme. Applicants should be prepared to discuss: Why they are interested in BRIDGE X. What social issues they care about. Their previous community or extracurricular involvement. Examples of leadership or initiative. How they have contributed to solving a problem. What they hope to learn from the programme. How they would engage their university campus. How they would balance BRIDGE X responsibilities with their studies. Successful participants will receive formal confirmation and onboarding information before beginning their BRIDGE X journey. How the Year-Long BRIDGE X Journey Works BRIDGE X is designed as a year-long exposure journey rather than a single event. Participants will take part in planned sessions, workshops and activities throughout the year while continuing with their university studies. This structure is important because it allows students to build their capabilities progressively. Instead of receiving a one-time introduction to development work, participants can have repeated opportunities to: Learn. Apply what they learn. Engage with others. Reflect on development challenges. Develop ideas. Lead campus activities. Expand their professional networks. Explore future career possibilities. Balancing BRIDGE X With University Studies The programme recognises that participants are undergraduate students who have existing academic responsibilities. BRIDGE X therefore involves planned activities that participants undertake while continuing their university education. Applicants should consider their existing academic workload and extracurricular commitments before applying. Students should be prepared to manage their time effectively and maintain a balance between the following: Academic coursework Examinations Assignments BRIDGE X activities Campus engagement Other extracurricular commitments Good time management and reliability will be important for students who are selected. Is BRIDGE X a Paid Opportunity? The information provided for the programme does not state that BRIDGE X is a paid programme . Applicants should therefore not assume that they will receive a salary, stipend, or other financial compensation unless BRAC confirms this separately. The programme s stated value centres on exposure, learning, networking, professional development, social-impact experience, and potential future pathways. Does BRIDGE X Guarantee an Internship or Job? No. Participation in BRIDGE X should not be interpreted as a guaranteed internship or employment offer. However, the programme can provide valuable exposure to BRAC, development practice, and professional networks, while potentially supporting participants as they explore future internship and early-career opportunities. Applicants should therefore view BRIDGE X primarily as a development and exposure opportunity , rather than a guaranteed recruitment programme. Why Students Interested in Development Should Consider Applying The development sector requires professionals who can understand complex problems, work with different stakeholders, and develop practical solutions. Students who gain exposure early can begin developing these capabilities before graduation. BRIDGE X can be particularly relevant to students interested in: Sustainable development Poverty reduction Social innovation Community development Youth empowerment International development Social enterprise Public policy Humanitarian and development work Non-governmental organisations Social entrepreneurship Global affairs Communications for development Leadership and civic engagement BRAC s broader work spans numerous development areas, including education, livelihoods, health, migration, climate resilience, and other social-development challenges. How to Prepare a Strong BRIDGE X Application Applicants should avoid submitting a generic application that simply states that they want to help people. Instead, they should demonstrate their motivation through specific experiences. 1. Clearly explain your motivation Explain why development and social impact matter to you. Connect your motivation to an issue, experience, project, course, volunteer activity, or community experience that has influenced your interests. 2. Demonstrate initiative Use concrete examples. For example, describe a time when you: Started an initiative. Organised an event. Volunteered in your community. Led a student project. Supported a social campaign. Helped address a community challenge. Mobilised other students around an issue. 3. Show what you have learned Do not only describe what you did. Explain what the experience taught you and how it changed your understanding of leadership or social impact. 4. Demonstrate problem-solving ability BRIDGE X involves solving development cases, so applicants should demonstrate that they can examine a problem carefully and think about practical solutions. 5. Explain what you will contribute Applicants should consider what they can bring to the programme. This could include: Leadership Research Communication Technology Community mobilisation Advocacy Creativity Entrepreneurship Project management Public speaking 6. Explain how you will engage your campus Because the programme involves campus activation, applicants should think about how they would create meaningful conversations at their university. Ideas could include: Development-focused seminars Student workshops Awareness campaigns Panel discussions Peer-learning sessions Social-impact challenges Student-led community initiatives BRIDGE X and Youth Leadership One of the programme s strongest themes is youth leadership. Rather than positioning young people solely as future beneficiaries of development, BRIDGE X provides a platform through which students can contribute ideas and perspectives today. Participants can become connectors between: University learning → Development practice → Youth engagement → Campus action → Social impact This makes the programme relevant to students who want to develop leadership capabilities while still at university. BRIDGE X and Career Development Early career development is another major element of the programme. Students often graduate with academic qualifications but limited understanding of professional environments. Exposure programmes can help close this gap by introducing students to practitioners, workplace expectations, and real-world problem-solving. Through BRIDGE X, participants can potentially strengthen transferable skills that are useful across many career paths, including: Communication Teamwork Leadership Problem-solving Critical thinking Presentation Networking Stakeholder engagement Event coordination Initiative Professional confidence These skills can remain useful regardless of the participant s eventual career sector. Important Deadline for BRIDGE X 2026 The application deadline is: 26 August 2026 Applicants should complete and submit their applications before the deadline. It is advisable not to wait until the final day, particularly because applicants may need time to prepare information about their university activities, leadership experiences, volunteering, motivation, and other relevant experiences. How to Apply for BRIDGE X 2026 Interested students should apply through the official BRIDGE X application process provided by BRAC. Application deadline: 26 August 2026 Official programme: BRAC BRIDGE X Programme Application form: BRIDGE X Application Form Applicants should carefully review the information requested in the application form and ensure that all required information is complete and accurate before submitting. APPLY HERE Key Takeaways for Prospective Applicants Before applying, prospective applicants should remember the following: BRIDGE X is a year-long exposure programme . It is designed for undergraduate university students . Students in their second or third year are specifically targeted. Students from any academic discipline can be considered. Demonstrated involvement in social, community, volunteering, club or co-curricular activities is important. Participants will be expected to engage with development challenges . Participants can help organise or facilitate campus-based activities . Selected students will serve as BRIDGE X focals . The programme provides opportunities for networking and professional development . Participants may gain exposure to global conferences and learning spaces . The programme does not guarantee an internship or job with BRAC. The information provided does not indicate that BRIDGE X is a paid programme. The application deadline is 26 August 2026 . Applicants should prepare to demonstrate their initiative, motivation, leadership, and interest in social development . Visit HERE for more information about the BRIDGE X Youth Exposure Programme 2026. Conclusion The BRIDGE X 2026 programme offers undergraduate students an opportunity to move beyond traditional academic learning and gain practical exposure to social development, social innovation, leadership and professional life. By bringing together problem-solving, campus engagement, networking, professional development, and exposure to BRAC s development ecosystem, the programme is designed to help young people understand how ideas can be transformed into action. For students who are already involved in university clubs, volunteering, community initiatives, or other social-impact activities, BRIDGE X can provide a structured environment in which to deepen those interests and develop them into practical leadership capabilities. The programme also offers an opportunity to build relationships with peers and practitioners, explore development-sector career pathways, and contribute youth perspectives to important social challenges. Students who meet the stated criteria and are genuinely interested in making a positive contribution should consider preparing their applications early. With the 26 August 2026 deadline approaching, prospective applicants should focus on demonstrating not only what they have achieved but also why they care about social change, what they have learned from their experiences, and how they intend to use the BRIDGE X experience to create meaningful impact on their campuses and beyond. title: ACET Young Leaders in Research (YLR) Grant 2026: Up to $15,000 for Early-Career African Researchers

Young Researchers receive funding, mentorship, visibility, and professional development support to elevate their research and influence policymaking on the continent. title: EU Delegation Policy Assistant Job in New York: Salary Up to $97,000, Eligibility, Requirements and How to Apply
summary: The European Union Delegation to the United Nations in New York is inviting applications for a Policy Assistant position in the Political 4 – UN Horizontal Issues Section , offering qualified professionals an opportunity to work at the intersection of international relations, United Nations affairs, diplomacy, public administration, policy analysis and multilateral negotiations. The position is based at the EU Delegation to the United Nations in New York , located at 666 Third Avenue, New York, NY 10017. The successful candidate will support the EU s work on a range of UN horizontal issues, particularly matters relating to accountability, administration, oversight mechanisms, internal justice and financial and budgetary issues. mThe position is particularly relevant to professionals with experience in public administration, international relations, UN affairs, policy analysis, diplomacy, multilateral negotiations or related fields who already have valid authorization to work in the United States. According to the vacancy information, the expected starting date is October 1, 2026 , while applications must be submitted no later than August 21, 2026, at noon Eastern Time . About the European Union Delegation to the United Nations in New York The European Union is an economic and political partnership consisting of 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development assistance and cooperation with international organizations. Outside the European Union, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations known as EU Delegations , which perform functions comparable in some respects to those of embassies. The EU Delegation to the United Nations in New York works as an observer with enhanced status and coordinates closely with the EU Member States so that the European Union can present common positions in the United Nations system. The Delegation also works closely with the UN Secretariat and its agencies, funds and programmes on global challenges and international policy issues. Policy Assistant, Political 4 – UN Horizontal Issues The vacancy is for a Policy Assistant in the Political 4 – UN Horizontal Issues Section , covering areas including: United Nations General Assembly affairs. Economic and Social Council-related issues. Administration. Financial and budgetary matters. UN accountability. UN oversight mechanisms. Internal justice and appeals. Policy and strategy development. Political analysis and reporting. Coordination with EU Member States and EU institutions. The successful applicant will be recruited as a Local Agent Group II . The initial contract is for two years , with the possibility of two renewals. Under successive fixed-term contracts, the maximum employment term can reach seven years . The vacancy information also indicates that an indefinite contract may be possible after completion of the seven-year period, subject to budget availability and operational considerations. The position is situated within a small team and may occasionally require atypical or flexible working hours. What Will the Policy Assistant Do? The person selected for the position will work under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the UN Horizontal Issues Section. The role focuses substantially on supporting the EU s work concerning UN accountability and oversight mechanisms , including both internal and external oversight structures. The responsibilities include providing support, expertise and assistance on matters involving: The Office of Internal Oversight Services (OIOS). The UN Joint Inspection Unit (JIU). The UN system of administration of justice. Internal justice and appeal mechanisms. The activities of the UN Ethics Office. System-wide strategies concerning the internal organization and accountability of the United Nations. The exact responsibilities may change depending on the evolving needs and priorities of the Delegation. Main Responsibilities and Duties 1. Supporting UN General Assembly Fifth Committee Negotiations One of the central responsibilities will be assisting the Head of Section in coordinating experts from EU Member States during intergovernmental negotiations on matters appearing on the agenda of the UN General Assembly Fifth Committee . The successful candidate will primarily focus on accountability-related issues while also providing support on other agenda items when necessary. Relevant areas include: The UN System of Administration of Justice. Joint Inspection Unit reviews and its annual programme of work. The Office of Internal Oversight Services. Administration of internal justice. Activities of the Ethics Office. This means the role requires an understanding of multilateral policymaking and the ability to follow complex negotiations involving numerous governments and international stakeholders. 2. Representing the European Union When necessary, the Policy Assistant may represent the EU on behalf of the Head of Section. This responsibility requires professionalism, confidence, strong communication skills and an ability to understand and communicate EU positions accurately in an international diplomatic environment. 3. Drafting Policy Language The successful candidate will draft policy language for negotiations and assist with consultations involving: The EU27. Like-minded countries where applicable. United Nations General Assembly negotiations. This requires excellent written communication, analytical thinking and the ability to turn complex policy matters into precise diplomatic language. 4. Preparing Reports and Political Assessments The Policy Assistant will contribute to reports, analyses and political assessments for EU headquarters. These materials will cover developments within the United Nations, negotiations, meetings and other issues under the responsibility of the section. The role may also involve monitoring broader horizontal matters, including coverage of the UN General Assembly General Debate . Additional Coordination Responsibilities Beyond the core UN accountability portfolio, the position includes several coordination and analytical responsibilities carried out in close consultation with the Press, Information and Coordination Section. These include supporting the preparation of: Policy and strategy papers. Analytical materials on horizontal issues. Political issue and process mappings. Materials for consideration by EU Deputy Permanent Representatives. Briefings and documentation relating to UN activities. The successful applicant will therefore need to be comfortable working across multiple files and coordinating information from different sources and stakeholders. Supporting the UN General Assembly High-Level Week Another important part of the position involves preparations for the UN General Assembly Ministerial/High-Level Week . The Policy Assistant will support preparations by: Covering UN consultations and preparations. Drafting speaking points. Preparing reports. Drafting correspondence. Developing planning overviews for high-level events. Working with EU headquarters and EU Member States. The successful candidate will also create and maintain comprehensive overviews and statistics concerning the alignment of EU candidate countries with EU statements at the United Nations and their voting patterns. Annual Management and Reporting Responsibilities The position also contributes to internal EU Delegation planning and reporting processes. The successful applicant will assist with the coordination and consolidation of inputs for: The Annual Management Plan of the EU Delegation. The annual Delegation record of achievements under Lisbon Treaty obligations. Statistical tables. Reporting requests from EU headquarters. Other cross-sectional coordination requirements. The Policy Assistant may additionally contribute to briefing documents and speaking points for the Head of Delegation and Deputy Head of Delegation for bilateral meetings and discussions at the United Nations. Workplace and Location The position is based at: EU Delegation to the United Nations 666 Third Avenue New York, NY 10017, USA The Delegation describes the working environment as collegial and international, with close cooperation with the Administration team and support for colleagues throughout the EU Delegation. The role is full-time and in person , with a working schedule of 37.5 hours per week . Salary and Benefits The position offers a competitive salary based on relevant and verified employment experience. The stated salary levels include approximately: $89,000 starting level for candidates with around 2 years of experience. $93,000 for around 6 years of experience. $97,000 for around 10 years of experience. The vacancy also lists a competitive benefits package. The listed benefits include: Personal leave days. Public holidays. Flexible working hours. Health insurance. Dental insurance. Vision insurance. Retirement savings plan. 401(k) matching. Paid time off. Flexible scheduling. The job listing gives a monthly pay range of approximately $7,600 to $9,000 , depending on the applicable employment terms and experience. Expected Start Date The expected starting date for the successful candidate is: October 1, 2026. Minimum Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy the minimum requirements for their application to be considered. Educational Qualification Applicants must have: A Bachelor s degree . A Master s degree is considered an asset. Professional Experience Candidates must have at least: Two years of professional experience in public administration and/or international relations. The vacancy specifies that the relevant professional experience must have been obtained after the date on which the applicant obtained the qualification that allows access to the position. Language Requirement Applicants must have a thorough working knowledge of: Written English Spoken English Strong written and oral communication skills are particularly important because the position involves drafting policy language, reports, analyses, correspondence, briefing notes and speaking points. A Critical Eligibility Requirement: U.S. Work Authorization One of the most important points applicants should understand before applying is the position s requirement concerning authorization to work in the United States. The EU Delegation states that it does not sponsor visas for Local Agents . Applicants therefore need to already possess valid U.S. work authorization that does not require sponsorship from the Delegation. Examples identified in the vacancy include: An Employment Authorization Document (EAD). A Green Card. U.S. citizenship. Certain G1 or G3 visas applicable to spouses of EU officials posted at an EU Member State Mission to the United Nations. This means that simply meeting the academic and professional requirements does not necessarily make an applicant eligible. The applicant must also satisfy the U.S. work authorization requirement. Preferred Skills and Selection Criteria Beyond the minimum requirements, the EU Delegation has identified several qualities and competencies that will be used when selecting the strongest candidates. Flexibility The successful candidate should be willing to work flexible hours when required. This is particularly relevant because the position involves international diplomacy and United Nations activities, where meetings, negotiations and high-level events may sometimes require working outside conventional hours. Ability to Work Independently and as Part of a Team Candidates should demonstrate the ability to: Work independently. Operate with minimal supervision. Collaborate effectively with colleagues. Contribute constructively to team objectives. Strong Coordination Skills The role requires strong coordination capabilities, including the ability to: Listen actively. Consult effectively. Share information. Exchange ideas. Coordinate with colleagues and stakeholders. Communication and Analytical Skills Applicants should be able to communicate complex issues clearly and effectively, both orally and in writing. The successful candidate should also be capable of: Producing high-quality briefing notes. Preparing reports. Writing analytical documents. Explaining complex matters in accessible language. Conducting political and policy analysis. Digital and Technology Skills The vacancy also emphasizes the ability to adapt to new technologies and digital tools. Candidates should therefore be comfortable learning and using modern digital systems relevant to policy, administration, communication, research and coordination. Interpersonal Skills The successful applicant should have excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrate: A positive attitude. A proactive approach. A solution-oriented mindset. The ability to remain calm under pressure. The ability to collaborate effectively in an international environment. Cultural Awareness Openness to cultural diversity is specifically identified as a selection criterion. This is particularly relevant to a position operating within an international diplomatic environment involving EU Member States, United Nations institutions and representatives from countries around the world. Problem-Solving Candidates should demonstrate strong problem-solving abilities, including the capacity to: Identify problems. Define the issues clearly. Gather relevant information. Analyze available information. Develop practical solutions. Implement effective responses. Organization and Time Management Because the position involves several files and responsibilities simultaneously, applicants should have excellent organizational and time-management skills. The successful candidate should be able to plan ahead, monitor implementation and follow up on multiple assignments. Additional Assets The following are considered additional advantages: Data analysis skills. Experience with the work of the UN General Assembly Fifth Committee. These are not presented as the minimum requirements but can strengthen an applicant s profile during the selection process. Documents Required for the Application Applicants must submit a complete application containing the required documentation. 1. Cover or Motivation Letter Applicants must provide a signed cover or motivation letter . This document should explain the applicant s interest in the position and demonstrate how their background and professional experience correspond to the requirements of the role. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a Curriculum Vitae containing, at minimum: Exact job titles. Names of employers. Detailed descriptions of tasks and responsibilities. The vacancy specifically requests the use of Europass CV templates . 3. Referees The CV must include the names and contact details of at least two referees who can attest to the applicant s professional and personal attributes if the applicant is shortlisted. 4. U.S. Work Authorization Applicants must indicate the type of U.S. work authorization they possess. The application should specify whether the applicant has, for example: A particular visa type. U.S. citizenship. A Green Card. An EAD. These application requirements are explicitly outlined in the vacancy notice. How to Apply Applicants should send their complete application to the designated EU Delegation recruitment email addresses provided in the vacancy notice. The application must be submitted to: eeasjobs-185@eeas.europa.eu and delegation-new-york-jobs@eeas.europa.eu The required email subject is: Ref: 455074 – JOB TITLE: Policy Assistant, UN Horizontal Issues Section Applicants should ensure that their application is complete before submission because missing required conditions or documents can result in rejection. Application Deadline The deadline for applications is August 21, 2026, at noon Eastern Time (EST) . Applicants should not wait until the final hours to prepare and submit their documents, particularly because the vacancy requires several pieces of information, including a signed motivation letter, detailed CV, referee information and proof or details of U.S. work authorization. What Happens After You Apply? After the application deadline, the applications will be reviewed by a Selection Committee established for the recruitment process. The committee will conduct a preliminary assessment based on the information provided in the: Cover or motivation letter. Curriculum Vitae. Other submitted application information. Candidates considered most suitable will be shortlisted and invited to an assessment phase that includes an interview . During this phase, the Selection Committee will assess the suitability of candidates for the position. Candidates who are not shortlisted will not be contacted individually at that stage. The Delegation will inform the remaining candidates after the recruitment procedure has been completed and a recruitment decision has been made. title: ITC SheTrades GRPP Policy Consultant 2026: Home-Based Consultancy Opportunity for Public Policy, Procurement and Agriculture Experts
summary: International Trade Centre (ITC) SheTrades GRPP Policy Consultant 2026 The International Trade Centre (ITC) is seeking a qualified National Consultant – Policy Consultant to support its SheTrades initiative and the development of a practical guide on gender-responsive public procurement (GRPP) for agricultural products . This home-based consultancy will contribute to an important initiative designed to help farmer organizations, women farmers, women-led agribusinesses and cooperatives better understand and access public procurement opportunities. The assignment will run from September to December 2026 , with the consultant expected to conduct research, develop a practical approximately 30-page guide, engage with farmer organizations and stakeholders, incorporate technical feedback, and deliver the final approved publication. The consultancy is particularly relevant for professionals with experience in public policy, governance, public procurement, agriculture, gender development, agricultural value chains, cooperatives, MSMEs, research, technical writing and knowledge-product development . Opportunity Overview The International Trade Centre is implementing this work through its Women and Trade Programme and SheTrades Initiative , with the objective of strengthening women s economic participation through trade and investment. The assignment forms part of ITC s broader work on gender-responsive public procurement , building on the successful implementation of the SheTrades: Promoting Gender-Responsive Public Procurement for Agricultural Products project in Ecuador. The initiative is now being scaled to Africa and Asia through the GIZ Global Programme Farmers Organisations for the Transformation of Agricultural and Food Systems (FO Hub). The selected consultant will help ITC produce a practical resource that can be used by farmer organizations and their members to better understand public procurement systems, prepare for tenders and improve their ability to participate in government procurement markets. Key details Organization: International Trade Centre (ITC) Programme: SheTrades Initiative / Women and Trade Programme Assignment: SheTrades GRPP – Policy Consultant Division/Section: Division of Sustainable and Inclusive Trade / Women, Youth, and Vulnerable Communities Section Type of assignment: National Consultant Contract type: Output Duty station: Home-based Duration: September to December 2026 Expected duration: Approximately four months Travel: No travel Main deliverable: Approximately 30-page practical guide Final deliverable deadline: December 4, 2026 Application deadline: The reference provided for this opportunity does not state a separate application deadline . Applicants should therefore verify the official ITC vacancy/consultancy notice for the current submission deadline before applying. About the International Trade Centre The International Trade Centre (ITC) is a joint agency of the United Nations and the World Trade Organization , headquartered in Geneva. ITC works to enable small businesses to succeed in international trade, particularly in developing and transition-economy countries. Its work involves providing sustainable and inclusive development solutions to: Private-sector businesses Trade support institutions Policymakers Entrepreneurs and business organizations Other stakeholders involved in international trade and economic development The organization focuses on helping businesses and institutions overcome barriers to international trade while supporting inclusive economic development. About the SheTrades Initiative The SheTrades Initiative was established by ITC to create an ecosystem of integrated solutions that support women s economic empowerment through greater participation in trade and investment. The initiative recognizes that increasing women s participation in trade requires more than simply providing individual businesses with opportunities. Women also need access to appropriate capacities, supportive markets, effective institutions and policies that do not create unnecessary barriers. SheTrades therefore works to help ensure that: Women have the capacities required to participate in trade. Women can access relevant markets and business opportunities. Support organizations can effectively assist women entrepreneurs. Market partners contribute to women s economic empowerment. Policies and trade systems become more inclusive. Inequalities within the trade policy environment that restrict women s participation are addressed. The Policy Consultant will contribute to this broader objective by helping develop practical guidance around gender-responsive public procurement , particularly in agricultural markets. Background to the Consultancy ITC is building on the successful implementation of its gender-responsive public procurement work in Ecuador, funded by GIZ. The organization is now expanding this work to Africa and Asia through the GIZ Global Programme Farmers Organisations for the Transformation of Agricultural and Food Systems (FO Hub). As part of this expansion, ITC is supporting three regional farmer organization networks: Eastern Africa Farmers Federation (EAFF) Asian Farmers Association for Sustainable Rural Development (AFA) West African Network of Peasants and Agricultural Producers (ROPPA) These organizations represent farmer communities and agricultural stakeholders across important regions. ITC s objective is to strengthen the ability of farmer organizations and their members to participate in public procurement markets, with particular attention to: Women farmers Women-led agribusinesses Agricultural cooperatives Farmer organizations Other agricultural suppliers The consultant will play a central role in converting technical information about public procurement into practical, accessible guidance that can be understood and used by the intended beneficiaries. What Is Gender-Responsive Public Procurement? Gender-responsive public procurement refers broadly to approaches that consider gender equality and women s economic participation within public purchasing processes. Governments purchase large quantities of goods and services through public procurement systems. For agricultural producers and businesses, these government markets can represent significant commercial opportunities. However, farmers, cooperatives, MSMEs and women-led businesses can face barriers when attempting to participate in procurement processes. These barriers can include: Limited knowledge of procurement procedures Difficulty understanding tender requirements Lack of information about available opportunities Complex administrative processes Limited capacity to prepare bids Insufficient understanding of government purchasing systems Limited access to business support services Challenges associated with agricultural supply chains Structural inequalities affecting women-owned and women-led businesses The practical guide developed through this consultancy is intended to help address some of these knowledge and capacity gaps. Main Objective of the Consultancy The primary objective of the assignment is to develop a practical, accessible and context-specific guide on public procurement opportunities for farmer organizations and their members. The guide is expected to strengthen knowledge of public procurement systems and help the target audience become more prepared to participate in tenders and government markets. The consultant will work closely with ITC and the three regional farmer organization networks throughout the process. The final resource should not simply reproduce technical information. It must translate complex procurement concepts into clear and practical guidance that can be used by farmer organizations, women farmers, women-led agribusinesses and cooperatives . Regional Focus of the Assignment The consultancy has a broad geographical and regional focus. Research and content development will consider public procurement, inclusive procurement and agricultural procurement within: Western Africa Eastern Africa Asia The work will specifically take into account the contexts represented by: EAFF AFA ROPPA This means that the consultant will need to understand how public procurement systems, agricultural markets and relevant institutional environments may differ across regions. The guide should therefore provide practical and context-sensitive information rather than relying solely on a single-country procurement model. Key Responsibilities of the Policy Consultant The selected consultant will work under the ITC Women and Trade Programme and SheTrades Initiative . The consultant will report directly to the SheTrades Associate Economic Affairs Officer and work under the overall guidance of the Data and Policy Lead of the SheTrades Initiative . The responsibilities are divided into three major areas: research and content development, practical guide development, and coordination with stakeholders. 1. Research and Content Development The consultant will first undertake extensive background research to establish the technical foundation of the guide. Conduct a desk review The consultant will review relevant: Literature Tools Policies Existing guidance documents Public procurement resources Inclusive procurement materials Agricultural procurement resources Particular attention will be given to the regions represented by the participating farmer organizations. The research will cover relevant contexts in Western Africa, Eastern Africa and Asia . The purpose of this research is to ensure that the guide is based on reliable existing knowledge and is relevant to the realities faced by farmer organizations and agricultural suppliers. Identify priority procurement topics The consultant will identify and prioritize the most important: Public procurement topics Procurement challenges Procurement opportunities Barriers to participation Practical considerations for agricultural suppliers The analysis will pay particular attention to the experiences and needs of women suppliers . Identify practical examples and case studies The consultant will also identify useful: Examples Good practices Case studies Practical approaches Existing tools and resources These materials will be incorporated into the guide where appropriate. The goal is to make the guide more useful to its intended audience by showing how procurement concepts can work in practical situations. 2. Development of the Practical Guide One of the most important responsibilities of the consultant will be to write and develop the practical guide. The final guide is expected to be approximately 30 pages . The consultant will work from an outline developed by ITC in consultation with the participating farmer organizations. The guide must be practical and user-friendly The consultant will be expected to develop content that is: Clear Practical Accessible User-friendly Context-specific Relevant to agricultural stakeholders The intended audience includes: Farmer organizations Women farmers Women-led agribusinesses Cooperatives Agricultural suppliers Related private-sector stakeholders The consultant must be capable of taking complex technical information about public procurement and transforming it into guidance that non-technical audiences can understand and apply. Compliance with ITC standards The guide must also comply with ITC s: Editorial standards Branding requirements Style requirements Formatting requirements The consultant will therefore need strong drafting and editing abilities in addition to technical knowledge. Incorporating feedback The guide will go through multiple rounds of review. The consultant will need to: Submit drafts to ITC. Receive technical and editorial feedback. Incorporate comments. Participate in consultations. Revise the guide. Address additional stakeholder feedback. Finalize the document. Obtain ITC approval. The consultant must therefore be comfortable managing iterative drafting and review processes. 3. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement Stakeholder engagement is another significant part of the assignment. The consultant will participate in coordination meetings with ITC and relevant stakeholders to discuss: Structure of the guide Content Research findings Progress Draft versions Stakeholder feedback Required revisions The consultant will also coordinate closely with ITC staff to ensure that the guide is aligned with existing: SheTrades methodologies ITC publications ITC knowledge products Relevant programme approaches Consultation With Farmer Organizations An important part of the assignment involves direct engagement with representatives of EAFF, AFA and ROPPA . The consultant will present draft versions of the guide during online consultation or validation sessions. These sessions will be used to: Present draft content Gather feedback Discuss the structure of the guide Assess its practical applicability Identify gaps Document stakeholder recommendations Incorporate agreed changes into later drafts This makes stakeholder communication a critical part of the role. The successful candidate must therefore be able to listen to different stakeholders, facilitate discussions, document feedback accurately and translate recommendations into improvements to the final publication. Expected Outputs and Important Deadlines The consultancy contains three major output stages. Output 1 — September 30, 2026 By September 30, 2026 , the consultant is expected to have: Conducted background research. Reviewed relevant literature. Reviewed existing resources. Developed the first draft of the practical guide. Based the draft on the outline developed by ITC in consultation with farmer organizations. Incorporated ITC s initial comments. Ensured that the draft follows ITC editorial and style requirements. This stage establishes the research and initial content foundation for the guide. Output 2 — October 30, 2026 By October 30, 2026 , the consultant must: Submit the second draft of the practical guide. Follow the approved structure established by ITC. Incorporate practical examples. Include relevant regional context. Ensure compliance with ITC editorial, formatting and branding requirements. Present the second draft during an online consultation or pilot validation session. The consultation will involve representatives from: EAFF AFA ROPPA The purpose of this session is to gather feedback concerning: Content Structure Practical applicability Relevance to the intended audience Output 3 — December 4, 2026 The final output deadline is December 4, 2026 . By this date, the consultant must: Submit the final approximately 30-page practical guide. Incorporate ITC comments. Incorporate feedback gathered during consultations. Submit all editable source files. Submit supporting materials used in developing the guide. Address all final ITC comments. Obtain approval of the final deliverable from ITC. The final deliverable therefore represents the culmination of the research, drafting, consultation and revision process. Travel Requirements The assignment is explicitly listed as home-based , and no travel is required . This means the consultant will be expected to conduct the work remotely, including coordination and consultation activities. Online meetings and virtual consultation or validation sessions will form part of the stakeholder engagement process. Education Requirements Applicants are expected to have a postgraduate degree , with relevant fields including: Business administration Economics Public policy Development studies Law A related field The reference also states that extensive relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of a master s degree . Therefore, candidates who do not have the specified master s-level qualification may still potentially qualify if they can demonstrate substantial and directly relevant professional experience. Professional Experience Requirements The consultancy requires substantial professional experience. Applicants should have at least five years of experience in: Public policy Governance Related fields The experience should also include relevant exposure to areas such as: Gender Public procurement Agriculture This is an important requirement because the assignment combines policy analysis with practical procurement and agricultural-market considerations. Experience Developing Guides, Toolkits and Knowledge Products Applicants should have demonstrated experience developing practical knowledge resources such as: Guidance documents Manuals Toolkits Knowledge products Policy resources Practical guides The experience should ideally involve developing materials for audiences such as: Policymakers Business support organizations Private-sector stakeholders This requirement is particularly important because the core output of the consultancy is a practical guide rather than a purely academic research paper. Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate that they can turn research and technical information into useful, accessible resources. Desirable Experience Experience with the following areas is highly desirable: Farmer organizations Experience working directly with farmer organizations can help a candidate understand the operational realities and needs of agricultural producer groups. Agricultural value chains Knowledge of agricultural value chains is relevant because the guide will focus on agricultural procurement and the ability of producers and organizations to access government markets. Cooperatives Experience working with cooperatives is valuable because cooperatives are among the intended beneficiaries of the guide. MSMEs Experience with micro, small and medium-sized enterprises is also desirable, particularly where procurement opportunities and market access are concerned. Gender development Experience in gender development is identified as an asset and is particularly relevant because the broader objective of the SheTrades Initiative is to promote women s economic participation. To apply, please send your CV/resumé to Ms. Gem Arbo darbo@intracen.org and Ms. Inês Aguiar Machado iaguiar@intracen.org by 28 August 2026. Required Skills The successful consultant is expected to demonstrate a combination of analytical, research, writing, communication and stakeholder-management skills. Excellent analytical skills The consultant must be capable of examining complex information and identifying the most relevant issues for the intended audience. Strong research skills The assignment involves extensive desk research covering policies, tools, literature, guidance and procurement practices across different regional contexts. Excellent drafting skills The consultant must be able to produce high-quality professional content suitable for an international organization. Ability to simplify complex information One of the most important skills for this assignment is the ability to transform technical information into practical and user-friendly guidance for non-technical audiences . This means the consultant must be able to explain procurement concepts clearly without unnecessarily complicated terminology. Knowledge of public procurement systems Strong knowledge of public procurement systems is required. Candidates should understand how public procurement processes operate and how suppliers can prepare to participate. Knowledge of agricultural markets The consultant should also have strong knowledge of agricultural markets and understand the circumstances affecting agricultural producers and organizations. Stakeholder consultation and communication The consultant must have excellent communication skills and be able to work effectively with: ITC staff Farmer organizations Technical stakeholders Programme representatives Other relevant partners Ability to work independently Because the assignment is home-based, the consultant must be capable of managing tasks independently while still responding effectively to feedback from multiple stakeholders. Ability to work under pressure The assignment involves multiple deadlines and several rounds of drafting and consultation. Applicants should therefore be able to maintain accuracy and quality while working under tight timelines. Attention to detail Attention to detail will be essential because the final guide must meet ITC s editorial, formatting, branding and technical requirements. Learn more about this opportunity HERE Language Requirements The consultancy has a specific language requirement. English Excellent proficiency in English, both spoken and written, is required. The consultant will need to conduct research, draft the guide, participate in meetings and communicate with stakeholders in English. French Excellent proficiency in French, both spoken and written, is also required. This makes bilingual English-French capability a key requirement for the assignment. Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate professional working proficiency in both languages.
